External stakeholders, including customers, regulators, and communities, increasingly expect manufacturers to adopt responsible and circular waste management practices, including reduction of hazardous waste and prevention of environmental contamination. Given Schaeffler India’s manufacturing footprint, effective waste management is material to meeting stakeholder expectations, regulatory compliance, and sustainability commitments. By focusing on waste reduction, reuse, and recycling, the Company is able to improve resource efficiency and support circular economy principles across its operations.

Cost optimisation through reduced waste disposal expenses and improved material efficiency; incremental revenue generation from the sale of recyclable waste streams (e.g., used oil, metal scrap); avoidance of regulatory penalties and environmental remediation costs. Strong waste management practices also support compliance, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability performance.
Positive implications as it helps reduce the long-term risk of non-compliance.

Increasing digitalisation of enterprise systems, including ERP, order management, and customer- specific engineering data, makes data security and privacy critical for Schaeffler India. Any data breach or cyber incident could expose sensitive commercial, technical, or personal information, disrupt operations, lead to non- compliance with applicable data protection regulations, and impact long-term customer trust and OEM relationships. Protecting customer and proprietary data is therefore essential for business continuity and reputation.

Schaeffler India addresses data security risks through a robust IT governance framework, supported by Group-wide information security policies aligned with ISO/IEC 27001 and industry standards. Controls include access management, regular security reviews, cyber threat monitoring through a Security Operations Centre (SOC), periodic audits, and employee awareness and training programmes. Incident response mechanisms are in place to ensure timely detection, containment, and remediation of cyber incidents.

Avoidance of potential financial losses arising from data breaches, including regulatory penalties, litigation costs, system downtime, loss of customer trust, and reputational damage. Ongoing investments in IT security infrastructure and governance help protect critical data assets, ensure operational resilience, and support long-term customer relationships.

High greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions pose several risks to the Company, including increased operational costs, regulatory compliance challenges, and reputational risks in a market with growing sustainability expectations. There is a potential risk arising from unmet stakeholder expectations regarding emissions management. Operational risks also include possible supply chain disruptions caused by climate change-related events. The Company depends on suppliers, primarily in the steel sector, to develop lower-carbon alternatives through research and development, which is critical for controlling the carbon footprint embedded in its products. Climate change presents both physical risks—such as acute and chronic impact on operations and the value chain—and transition risks, including technological changes, evolving market demands, and shifting policy landscapes.

Schaeffler recognizes the physical and transition risks of climate change over the short, medium, and long term. To address these risks, the Company is implementing measures to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the following areas: Direct emissions from its operations (Scope 1 and Scope 2). Indirect emissions within the supply chain (Scope 3). Additionally, Schaeffler actively engages with suppliers to identify and adopt sustainable alternatives that reduce emissions at the source. Since 2023, Schaeffler has adopted Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)-validated climate targets aligned with the Paris Agreement’s goal to limit global warming. Following the merger with Vitesco Technologies, these targets are currently under review to ensure continued alignment and revalidation by the SBTi.

Negative financial implications include increased operational costs driven by carbon pricing mandates and regulatory compliance requirements, which enhance transition risks. An increase in weather events such as storms, floods, and heatwaves could have significant direct and indirect impact on our supply chain and operations, potentially disrupting production and affecting our ability to fulfill demand. Additionally, policy directions requiring low-carbon manufacturing may necessitate capital investments and operational changes. Failure to meet stakeholder expectations on emissions management could lead to reputational damage and loss of market share. On the positive side, investments in emissions reduction and sustainable technologies can lead to cost savings through improved energy efficiency, resource optimisation, and reduced carbon footprint. Developing low-carbon products and adopting greener supply chain practices open new market opportunities and strengthen relationships with sustainability- focused customers. Aligning with global climate targets, such as the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), enhances investor confidence, supports access to sustainable financing, and positions the Company for long-term resilience.

Schaeffler India operates in the automotive and industrial segments where customers increasingly demand products that meet high standards of quality, safety, regulatory compliance, and environmental performance. Product quality and safety are critical to maintaining customer trust and long-term OEM relationships, while sustainable product design—through material efficiency, reduced environmental footprint, and end- of-life considerations—supports evolving regulatory requirements and customer sustainability expectations. Continuous R&D and technology-led innovation, aligned with Schaeffler Group’s global R&D agenda, enables the development of market-ready, safe, and sustainable products, strengthening competitiveness and supporting long-term growth.

Risks related to product failure, safety incidents, or non-compliance are mitigated through robust quality management systems, a strong safety and “zero-defect” culture, and group-wide product validation and approval processes. Sustainability considerations, including material compliance, reduced use of hazardous substances, and end-of-life (EoL) integration, are embedded in product design and development processes. Ongoing investments in R&D, innovation governance, and technology reviews ensure alignment with regulatory, customer, and Group sustainability requirements.

Positive financial implications include revenue growth through stronger OEM relationships, market access, and customer preference for safe and sustainable products; a pricing premium for high-performance and sustainable solutions; enhanced competitiveness driven by innovation; optimisation of lifecycle costs, contributing to sustained business value. Negative financial implications include incremental capital expenditure (capex) and operational expenditure (opex) related to R&D and design efforts; cost avoidance through the reduction of recalls, warranty claims, safety incidents, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage; and long-term value creation through innovation-led competitiveness and lifecycle cost optimisation.

Schaeffler India’s manufacturing operations involve significant engagement of employees and contract workers on the shop floor. Any workplace accident, injury, or unsafe working condition can have serious implications for employee well-being, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, and reputation. While the nature of operations limits exposure to highly hazardous substances, lapses in safety practices or unsafe conditions could still result in injuries, downtime, and non- financial impacts that are not easily reversible. Therefore, occupational health and safety remains a critical risk area requiring continuous management focus.

The Company has established comprehensive occupational health and safety management systems, supported by both proactive and reactive controls. These include regular safety audits, training and awareness programmes, incident reporting mechanisms, and defined investigation and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) processes for any incident. Corrective and preventive actions are systematically implemented to reduce recurrence. Continuous monitoring and leadership oversight help ensure adherence to safety standards and improvement in workplace conditions.

Losses arising from workplace accidents— including medical expenses, compensation payments, regulatory penalties, litigation costs, increased insurance premiums, and production downtime—are minimised through the implementation of robust safety controls. Proactive safety management not only ensures operational continuity and protects human capital but also helps prevent reputational damage and reduces indirect costs linked to lost productivity and employee turnover.

The Automotive Technologies division develops and manufactures innovative products, components, and systems solutions for engine, transmission, and chassis applications for ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), hybrid as well as electric powertrains.

The Bearings and Industrial Solutions division offers a wide range of products that include ball and roller bearings, plain bearings, bearing housings and accessories, linear bearings, and ultra precision drives. It also offers lubrication products that include grease and oils, maintenance products that include a wide range of mounting and dismounting tools, and condition monitoring systems to customers across various industrial sectors. These products are distributed through direct sales channels as well as through a widespread network of certified distribution partners.

The Vehicle Lifetime Solutions business supplies components and holistic repair solutions for the automobile spare parts business under the leading brands of LuK, INA, and FAG. It offers comprehensive services to garages under the REPEXPERT brand to cater to the ever-changing customer needs.

• Permanent Workers: Worker unions are established, allowing employees to file complaints or approach management at any time to resolve their grievances effectively. • Non-Permanent Workers: External unions represent non- permanent workers. These workers raise personal or collective grievances, if any, through their appointed leaders, who escalate issues to the respective contractors and the Industrial Relations (IR) Head for amicable resolution. • Functional Management Responsibility: Functional managers are accountable for implementing, monitoring, and reporting Human Rights and Code of Conduct (CoC) related issues. They ensure timely management intervention where necessary. • Whistle-Blower and Vigil Mechanism: A defined policy supports complaint filing through dedicated email IDs, helpline numbers, and Single Points of Contact (SPOCs). Contact information is widely circulated among employees to facilitate awareness and ease of reporting. • Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Committees: Each plant and office has an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to address POSH-related concerns through helpline numbers, email IDs, and SPOCs. • Additional Feedback Channels for Permanent Employees: Mechanisms such as Town Hall Meetings, Open House Meetings, and “Skip to Succeed” interactive sessions are in place to receive employee feedback and grievances, ensuring responsive communication.
